97:- `record.md` carries, as complete findings, the FACTS entry the rung earns, its ledger notes, the whole new line of each row whose claim its change alters, its new rows, the handover line, and a "Revival change" section, or "Revival change: none" with the reason. The section is material for the skill writer, not skill text, in two labelled parts: "The change", as evidence (the team's source and what it says or does, with `file:line`; what the tree now does, with its test; the reason, as a passage, a checker refusal or a measured failure), and "Provenance" (the question or item, the answer or default it follows, the batch). The worker is told: "Name no question, item, batch, rung or record file in the change, and give no decision's status there; provenance goes in its own part." (the `coordinator` skill's `references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method"; `reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "Proposed fix to the mechanism", item 2.)
98-- `REPORT.md` opens with five provenance lines: problem, spec, precedent, deviation, historical. The `historical:` line names every file of the 2012 tree the rung edits, for the commit message (the protocol's hard rule on the gate).
99-- The worker does not edit FACTS, the ledger, PLAN, POSITIONS, INDEX, the handover, the tools or `.claude/`: the gather folds `record.md` into them, since every rung would conflict there.
100-- It commits and pushes its own files on its branch as it goes, so a dead container loses nothing.
101-- Its result carries `reportText` and `recordText` word for word, since the harness often refuses a worker's write of those files; `decisions`, each with the ways not taken, which its skeptic weighs its fixes against; `pointsReached`; and `forCurator`, its questions for the curator.
102-- A point to report is listed with its evidence, and the rung lands. Only a step that cannot be undone or acts against a decision on record is not taken: the worker stops and says which (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs").
103-
104-A rung that edits only prose has no test and no failure to see. Its text is checked against the tree and the decisions on record. A `testIsStage` rung's test is the checker count or distance stage, run once after its edit and rebuild, its before the last landed gate's table. A rung that changes the compiled checker also times the count stage on the base build before its edit and on its tree once the change is correct, in one session, then makes the second pass that the skill's `compiler.md`, "The checker's time", asks for, which makes the checker faster and keeps its results the same; the brief says that section holds where the brief differs (P-148, "The checker's speed comes right after its correctness.").
105-
106-## Skeptic
107-
108-The skeptic checks the rung and fixes what it finds, so that the rung lands right with no repair round after it (`process-engineering/batch-redesign.md`, "The skeptic that fixes what it finds").
109-
--
160:- **The record folded.** The FACTS entry under its area. A ledger note that adds a fact through `ledger.py note`. A change to what a row says (its claim narrowed, a half fixed, its test promoted or renamed, its notes at the limit) through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`: the whole line, stating the gap as it stands now, not its repair history. A note refused for length goes in so, with the notes cut back; none is left out. New rows through `ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE`, each `NEW-<rung>-<n>` placeholder replaced with its number everywhere the rung's files and tests cite it, before the rung's commit. The handover line, in the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Handover lines" (the old handover file is retired into PLAN's first section, which the coordinator keeps). The rung's "Revival change" section is folded into no file: both its parts are copied, word for word, into the batch's `RECORD.md` (below), and nothing is written under `.claude/`. Through batch 13 the gather folded each entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md` as the rung wrote it, and the cold reader that followed made a question's handle findable instead of deleting it: that is how the coordinator's agenda reached the skill (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there").
161-- **Corrections still owed.** The skeptic's `leftForGather` items. Each sentence of the specification a rung lists as made false and did not edit, corrected to what the code does, each clause checked against its code line. Batch 8's gather saw rung Q's Appendix I Effect false and let it stand, and in batch 9 no stage saw the one rung K made false. Each took a review judge and a repair, 0.53M and 0.39M (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 5; `reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6).
162-- **Text mismatches.** A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking ("Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 4).
163-- **Items for the curator.** The gather puts every item a rung, skeptic or judge returned into `PLAN.md`, under "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed" when work waits on it, else under "Off the path, parked".
164:- **After the rungs.** One commit closes each row a landed rung fixed (`ledger.py close N --commit HASH --test NAME`, then `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, which fails on any finding, also one the base already had; each is cleared through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or the entry reworded, before the commit). One commit writes the batch's `RECORD.md`, once, last: the order and why, each rung's commit, the rows opened and closed, each skeptic's fixes and the contested rulings by commit, the rungs that did not land, the points to report, where each item for the curator went, and last, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer", each landed rung's "Revival change" section, both parts word for word.
165-
166-A rung that did not land has its `REPORT.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` taken out of its branch path by path, its findings folded under "Not landed", and its new rows added. None of its source is applied.
167-
168-Files are staged by an explicit list and `git diff --cached --stat` is read before each commit. A commit touching a path outside `explorations/` and `.claude/` carries a `historical:` line.
169-
170-## Review beside the gate
171-
172-The review and the gate start together on the gather's commits. The review reads and never builds; the gate builds and never reads the record; the gate commits nothing, so the two never commit at once. Run side by side they took 14.7 minutes per batch off the serial tail. The review stays, once (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). Its six checks:
173-
174-1. Overlaps between rungs, and what their changes do together.
175-2. Each skeptic's fix and each repair commit, as applied: it does what its finding says, its test seen failing on the worker's head and then passing in its maker's transcript, a settled fix's citation, a reverted fix gone.
176-3. The folded record: FACTS lines, `ledger.py landing-check BASE` with no finding, also none the base already had, each fixed in the review's corrections commit, no `NEW-` placeholder left where a row is cited, every closed row fixed, the handover, the revival-change material in `RECORD.md` true of the landed code.
--
238:The batch writes no skill text. Each rung's "Revival change" material goes into the batch's `RECORD.md`, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer". After the landing, the standing skill writer writes the skill from it, and a cold read of the changed parts follows ("After the landing: the coordinator's routing", step 4). One writer does the writing (the `coordinator` skill's `references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method").
239-
240-Through batch 13 the gather folded each rung's entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md`, the review could correct it there, and a cold reader read it beside the gate's tail and made a handle findable instead of deleting it. That carried question handles, decision status and batch records into a part that workers load (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there"). The batch's cold reader and its `coldread.N` and `delta-unfolded.N` items are gone with the fold.
241-
242-The commit stage checks that nothing under `.claude/` changed since the base (step 2, below).
243-
244-## Commit, and the push held
245-
246-The commit stage:
247-
248-0. Starts the quick microGPT walk check in the background, unless an earlier attempt started it (`tools/mg-run.sh`, the quick pair, about a minute; P-30, "The check of microGPT under walk after a batch must take less than a minute."). It waits for the result before it returns. Unless both programs print `ALL PASS`, `microgpt-walk.1` is listed. It holds nothing.
249-1. Copies the gate's outputs into `compile-ladder/climb-batch-<N>/gate/` and the per-site list into place. It writes the landed figures into FACTS, numbers only: "The true distance to the switch-over" and "The checker-count stage's table". It builds the specification's PDF once if a landed commit changed `Specification/`.
250-   1a. Appends the repair runs and the paths no stage reads beside the summary, where the first gate's tables stand.
--
276:   - One task for the standing skill writer (`tools/skill-writer.sh`, its brief `skill-writer-brief.md`): the batch's revival-change material, the section "Revival changes, for the skill writer" of its `RECORD.md`; the skill sentences that the post-batch review lists as false; and any `skill-touched` item. The writer runs `tools/skills-lint.py` before each commit.
277-   - A cold read of the parts the writer changed, by an agent given only the skill and `skill-cold-read-brief.md`.
278-   - The writer fixes the cold read's flags, and the coordinator pushes its commits.
279-5. The next batch launched only after that, so that its workers read the updated skill (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
280-6. The combined post-batch review, started at the landing, since step 4 takes its list of false skill sentences (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
281-
282-The review explains every new or risen row of the checker count by a named rung edit. It reads the microGPT walk check's result. It reports the batch's measures against the batches before it with `tools/batch-measures.py` on the run's directory (`batch-redesign.md`, "The measures").
283-
284-## An agent that comes back with nothing
285-
286-Every `agent()` call goes through `callAgent`. A null result, an undefined one and a thrown error are treated alike, and the role runs up to two more times. A retry's prompt opens with a head saying an earlier attempt ended without its result, and listing what it may have left and how to continue from it:

Where a line it cites moved on `main`, the line on `main` follows the copy; then the skill sentences the rung's report lists as made false, which the batch does not edit.

209-### I (`rung-integer-power`, `5ad4a9957`)
210-
211-#### The change
212-
213-1. **An integer power's type, and its value at a negative exponent.**
214-   - The team's sources:
215-     - The library declared every integer `^` as answering `RR64`: `opr ^(self, b:AnyIntegral):RR64` on `Integral` and each integer type (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:721`, `:799-801`, `:892-894`, `:975-977`, `:1074-1076`; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:460-462`, `:552-554`, at `97ccd5f1f`).
216-     - Walk's natives answered the integer at a nonnegative exponent and `1.0 / pow(base, -exp)` at a negative one (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:220-230` and its five kin, at `97ccd5f1f`): `2^(-1)` was `0.5` and `0^(-1)` was `Infinity`.
217-     - The Working Draft gave `2^(-1)` as `1/2` through the rational power (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/numbers.tex:344-355`).
218-     - The compiler's prelude types the `ZZ32` power `ZZ32` at a `ZZ32` exponent (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:267`), and answers 0 at a negative one (row 523).
219-   - What the tree now does:
220-     - Each integer `^` answers its base's own type (under walk the numeral object's power answers a `ZZ32` value, as all its arithmetic does; row 578).
221-     - The compiled path's own library still answers 0 at a negative exponent, and a Java exception no `catch` sees at a base of 0 (rows 441 and 523; `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXIntegerPowerContractCompiled.test`).
222-     - At a negative exponent the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power, 0 raises `DivisionByZero`, and any other base raises `IntegerOverflow`.
223-     - A fraction is written with a float or rational base, `2.0^(-1)`.
224-     - The integer chapter's method entry says so (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:534-539`).
225-     - Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/IntegerPowerContractWalk.fss`.
226-   - The reason:
227-     - The compiled checker refuses the library as written: 'Function body has type RR64, but declared return type is QQ.' in the rational power (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:642` at `97ccd5f1f`), and 'ZZ32->ZZ32 is not applicable to an argument of type RR64' in `strToFloat` (`:4556`). On the flat tower an `RR64` holds no integer value.
228-     - The team's later code types an integer power by its integer at a signed exponent (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:267`).
229-     - No type carries the sign of a numeral, so no overload can tell `10^16` from `10^(-16)`: the checker types every integer numeral `IntLiteral` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:468-469`).
230-2. **The rational power over any integer.**
231-   - The team's library: `if -other > 0 then (denominator(self)/numerator(self))^(-other) else (numerator(self))^other / (denominator(self))^other end` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:641-646` at `97ccd5f1f`), under the comment "Way too clever by half". The api declared its exponent `ZZ64` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:430`).
232-   - What the tree now does: a `typecase` over the five integer types negates only inside a signed type (`fss:641-648`), and the api takes `AnyIntegral` (`fsi:431`). Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/QQPowerExponent.fss`, `RationalTest.fss`.
233-   - The reason: the checker's 'Could not check call to operator -', since `AnyIntegral` declares no `-` (`fss:642`, `:643` at `97ccd5f1f`). Under walk an unsigned exponent's negation wraps, so it recursed (row 445).
234-3. **`strToInt`'s `fail`.**
235-   - The team's library: `fail("strToInt(" … ")")` in the `else` of a generator clause inside `SUM[\ZZ32\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4543` at `97ccd5f1f`).

the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] The interpreter and the compiled type checker, when it checks
\library, read the rule and the exclusion by the qualified name of
\library's trait, so a program's own trait named \TYP{Index} is not read as
it, and both keep \TYP{Index} outside \TYP{Object}; a program with an index
type of its own declares it an \TYP{Index}.
A program's own generic declaration that instantiates an indexed type of
\library\ at its own type parameter bounds that parameter by \TYP{Index}; the
compiled type checker refuses it unbounded, ``The static argument \VAR{I} does
not satisfy the corresponding bound \TYP{Index}'', and the interpreter runs
it.
The compiled type checker refuses a tuple expression of indices passed to a
function whose one parameter's type is \TYP{Index}, as \EXP{f(i, j)} for
\EXP{f(x\COLON \TYP{Index})}, though it takes a variable of the tuple type
(row~NEW-B-1 of the revival's gap ledger); the interpreter runs it.
A numeral is no \TYP{Index} to the compiled type checker, which types it
\TYP{IntLiteral} (\secref{revival-numeral-type}); the interpreter, whose
numerals are values of the integer types (row~364), passes one to a parameter
of type \TYP{Index}.
The compiled path still compiles programs against its own library, which
declares no \TYP{Index}, until it is switched over to the interpreter's.
The code generator refuses a method with a \KWD{where} clause of its own
(row~701 of the revival's gap ledger), so after the switch-over
\TYP{BoundedRange}'s \VAR{atMost} waits on that row, beside the two
\VAR{distribute} methods of \library's sum reduction.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/types-vals-vars.tex},
lines 134--136, 215--216 and 272--273, which the change revises:
\begin{quote}
We say that a value is \emph{an instance of} its runtime type and of every
supertype of its runtime type; immediate subtypes of \TYP{Any} comprises of
tuple types, arrow types, \TYP{()}, and \TYP{Object}.

(* A tuple type whose element types are all Index types is an Index and no Object, so a static parameter bounded by Index takes ZZ32 and its pairs and triples, and the subscript beside the range subscript runs at each. *)
component TupleIndexBoundWalk
export Executable

ident[\I extends Index\](x: I): I = x

trait Cells[\I extends Index\]
    opr[i: I]: String
    opr[r: Range[\I\]]: String
end

object Grid[\I extends Index\]() extends Cells[\I\]
    opr[i: I]: String = "one index"
    opr[r: Range[\I\]]: String = "a range"
end

object Slot(n: ZZ32) extends Index end

kind(x: Object): String = "object"
kind(x: Any): String = "any"

oneIndex(x: Index): String = "an index"

run(): () = do
    assert(ident(3), 3, "ident takes a ZZ32 at its bound Index")

## Revival change

### The change

1. **A tuple of indices is an `Index`.**
   - The team's sources:
     - The Working Draft: "Every trait type also excludes every arrow type and every tuple type, and the special types () and BottomType." (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:215-216`) and "A tuple type excludes any non-tuple type other than Any." (`:272-273`).
     - The 2012 Types chapter: "Every trait type excludes \Void, \Bottom\ and every tuple type." (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick:341`) and "A tuple type excludes \Bottom, \Void, and every trait type, arrow type or function type." (`:424`).
     - The checker made a tuple exclude every trait type and be a subtype of none (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:329-330`, `:560` at `00f2e1bdc`); walk made a tuple a subtype of no trait and every trait exclude every tuple (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/types/FTypeTuple.java:107`, `FType.java:203-204` at `00f2e1bdc`).
     - The library left the index parameter unbounded, `trait Indexed[\E, I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1260` at `00f2e1bdc`), and the team's appendix of proposed features wanted "a type, say, Index which either excludes Range[I] or is a supertype of Range[I]", blocked because "we write a[1, 2, 3] where the arguments are passed as a tuple", needing "a magic to convert that tuple argument expression to something of type Index" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/future.tex:200-207`).
   - What the tree now does:
     - `trait Index extends Any end` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1245`); `ZZ32` extends it (`:533`); `Range` excludes it (`:2189`); every index parameter of the generic indexed types is `I extends Index` (`:1266` and the rest), and `Random`'s `UniformDistribution[\T extends Index\]` (`Library/Random.fsi:260`).
     - A tuple type whose element types are all subtypes of `Index` is a subtype of `Index`, and excludes `Index` only where one of its element types does: in the checker (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:331-333`, `:565-567`), in walk (`FTypeTuple.java:130`, `:200-201`, `:219-220`, `:412-422`; `FType.java:205`), and in the specification (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:335-351`, `:238-246`). `()` is no `Index`.
     - `m[i, j]` passes its tuple `(i, j)` as before. The rule reads the library's trait by its qualified name, `FortressLibrary.Index`; a program's own trait `Index` is not it.
     - A program's generic over an indexed type's index parameter bounds it by `Index`: the checker refuses `f[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\])`, 'Ill-formed type: Array[\RR64,I\] The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Index.'; walk runs it.
     - The checker refuses a tuple expression of indices at a function whose one parameter's type is `Index` (row NEW-B-1), and a numeral there, which it types `IntLiteral`; walk runs both.
     - Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/TupleIndexBoundWalk.fss`; the checker's half: the full check of symbolic operators, whose 124 subscript errors are gone.
   - The reason:
     - Unbounded, `opr[i: I]` beside `opr[r: Range[\I\]]` is invalid at `I = Any`: the range subscript is the more specific there, and its result is no element (row 783). The checker, reading symbolic operators, refused the pair at 124 sites of the library.
     - With the bound and no rule, the checker refuses the tuple indices, 'does not satisfy the corresponding bound Index' at `(ZZ32, ZZ32)` and `(ZZ32, ZZ32, ZZ32)` (73 sites), and walk stops at the first pair: '** bug! Meet((Int,Int), Index) not a singleton: []' (`TupleIndexBoundWalk` run with the base's `FTypeTuple` and `FType`).
     - A conversion, the team's word, would change each index value that a subscript passes; the rule changes no value.
2. **`Index` stands outside `Object`.**
   - The team's sources: "every trait except Any and Object implicitly extends the trait Object if it does not do so explicitly" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex:181-183`), and the hierarchy "rooted at trait Object" (`:193-194`); the desugarer made every trait that names nothing but `Any` extend `Object` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/desugarer/PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:76` at `00f2e1bdc`); the checker made every trait type an `Object` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:260` at `00f2e1bdc`); the specification's library declares its trait of all tuples outside `Object`, `trait Tuple extends Any excludes { Object }` (`Specification/basic-lib/objects.tex:180-186`).
   - What the tree now does: `Index` extends only `Any`; the desugarer keeps it so (`PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:127-130`, `:169-171`) and the checker's shortcut excepts it (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:261-262`); a pair of indices is an `Index` and no `Object` on both paths (`TupleIndexBoundWalk`: `instanceOf[\Object\]((1, 2))` is `false`, `kind((1, 2))` runs `kind(x: Any)` beside `kind(x: Object)`); a trait, object or object expression whose `extends` clause names only `Index` (and `Any`) extends `Object` beside it (`PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:91-123`; `TupleIndexBoundWalk`'s `Slot`); the specification, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:186-210`.
   - The reason: an unbounded type parameter is bounded by `Any`, which holds tuples where `Object` does not; were `Index` an `Object`, a tuple of indices would be an `Object`, or the subtype relation would not be transitive at `Index`. The checker over a program with `x: I`, `I extends Index`: 'Object->ZZ32 is not applicable to an argument of type I.'; over `object Slot(n: ZZ32) extends Index end`, `takesObject(s)` is accepted.
3. **`BoundedRange`'s narrowed `atMost` holds only at an index type.**
   - The team's library: `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\]` in `BoundedRange[\I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2251`, `.fss:4099` at `00f2e1bdc`).
   - What the tree now does: `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\] where { I extends Index }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2257`, `.fss:4105`); walk loads and runs it as before (`ant testSystem`, 669 tests, 0 failures).
   - The reason: `FullRange` takes the bound and `BoundedRange` cannot, since `Range`'s `truncL` and `truncR` return a `BoundedRange` and the open range `(:)` is a range over `Any`; written without the condition, the checker refuses the line: 'Ill-formed type: FullRange[\I\] The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Index.' After the switch-over the code generator's refusal of a method with a `where` clause of its own (row 701) reaches it, beside the sum reduction's two `distribute`s.

## Revival change

### The change

1. **A tuple of indices is an `Index`.**
   - The team's sources:
     - The Working Draft: "Every trait type also excludes every arrow type and every tuple type, and the special types () and BottomType." (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:215-216`) and "A tuple type excludes any non-tuple type other than Any." (`:272-273`).
     - The 2012 Types chapter: "Every trait type excludes \Void, \Bottom\ and every tuple type." (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick:341`) and "A tuple type excludes \Bottom, \Void, and every trait type, arrow type or function type." (`:424`).
     - The checker made a tuple exclude every trait type and be a subtype of none (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:329-330`, `:560` at `00f2e1bdc`); walk made a tuple a subtype of no trait and every trait exclude every tuple (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/types/FTypeTuple.java:107`, `FType.java:203-204` at `00f2e1bdc`).
     - The library left the index parameter unbounded, `trait Indexed[\E, I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1260` at `00f2e1bdc`), and the team's appendix of proposed features wanted "a type, say, Index which either excludes Range[I] or is a supertype of Range[I]", blocked because "we write a[1, 2, 3] where the arguments are passed as a tuple", needing "a magic to convert that tuple argument expression to something of type Index" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/future.tex:200-207`).
   - What the tree now does:
     - `trait Index extends Any end` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1245`); `ZZ32` extends it (`:533`); `Range` excludes it (`:2189`); every index parameter of the generic indexed types is `I extends Index` (`:1266` and the rest), and `Random`'s `UniformDistribution[\T extends Index\]` (`Library/Random.fsi:260`).
     - A tuple type whose element types are all subtypes of `Index` is a subtype of `Index`, and excludes `Index` only where one of its element types does: in the checker (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:331-333`, `:565-567`), in walk (`FTypeTuple.java:130`, `:200-201`, `:219-220`, `:412-422`; `FType.java:205`), and in the specification (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:335-351`, `:238-246`). `()` is no `Index`.
     - `m[i, j]` passes its tuple `(i, j)` as before. The rule reads the library's trait by its qualified name, `FortressLibrary.Index`; a program's own trait `Index` is not it.
     - A program's generic over an indexed type's index parameter bounds it by `Index`: the checker refuses `f[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\])`, 'Ill-formed type: Array[\RR64,I\] The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Index.'; walk runs it.
     - The checker refuses a tuple expression of indices at a function whose one parameter's type is `Index` (row NEW-B-1), and a numeral there, which it types `IntLiteral`; walk runs both.
     - Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/TupleIndexBoundWalk.fss`; the checker's half: the full check of symbolic operators, whose 124 subscript errors are gone.
   - The reason:
     - Unbounded, `opr[i: I]` beside `opr[r: Range[\I\]]` is invalid at `I = Any`: the range subscript is the more specific there, and its result is no element (row 783). The checker, reading symbolic operators, refused the pair at 124 sites of the library.
     - With the bound and no rule, the checker refuses the tuple indices, 'does not satisfy the corresponding bound Index' at `(ZZ32, ZZ32)` and `(ZZ32, ZZ32, ZZ32)` (73 sites), and walk stops at the first pair: '** bug! Meet((Int,Int), Index) not a singleton: []' (`TupleIndexBoundWalk` run with the base's `FTypeTuple` and `FType`).
     - A conversion, the team's word, would change each index value that a subscript passes; the rule changes no value.
2. **`Index` stands outside `Object`.**
   - The team's sources: "every trait except Any and Object implicitly extends the trait Object if it does not do so explicitly" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex:181-183`), and the hierarchy "rooted at trait Object" (`:193-194`); the desugarer made every trait that names nothing but `Any` extend `Object` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/desugarer/PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:76` at `00f2e1bdc`); the checker made every trait type an `Object` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:260` at `00f2e1bdc`); the specification's library declares its trait of all tuples outside `Object`, `trait Tuple extends Any excludes { Object }` (`Specification/basic-lib/objects.tex:180-186`).
   - What the tree now does: `Index` extends only `Any`; the desugarer keeps it so (`PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:127-130`, `:169-171`) and the checker's shortcut excepts it (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:261-262`); a pair of indices is an `Index` and no `Object` on both paths (`TupleIndexBoundWalk`: `instanceOf[\Object\]((1, 2))` is `false`, `kind((1, 2))` runs `kind(x: Any)` beside `kind(x: Object)`); a trait, object or object expression whose `extends` clause names only `Index` (and `Any`) extends `Object` beside it (`PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:91-123`; `TupleIndexBoundWalk`'s `Slot`); the specification, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:186-210`.
   - The reason: an unbounded type parameter is bounded by `Any`, which holds tuples where `Object` does not; were `Index` an `Object`, a tuple of indices would be an `Object`, or the subtype relation would not be transitive at `Index`. The checker over a program with `x: I`, `I extends Index`: 'Object->ZZ32 is not applicable to an argument of type I.'; over `object Slot(n: ZZ32) extends Index end`, `takesObject(s)` is accepted.
3. **`BoundedRange`'s narrowed `atMost` holds only at an index type.**
   - The team's library: `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\]` in `BoundedRange[\I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2251`, `.fss:4099` at `00f2e1bdc`).
   - What the tree now does: `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\] where { I extends Index }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2257`, `.fss:4105`); walk loads and runs it as before (`ant testSystem`, 669 tests, 0 failures).
   - The reason: `FullRange` takes the bound and `BoundedRange` cannot, since `Range`'s `truncL` and `truncR` return a `BoundedRange` and the open range `(:)` is a range over `Any`; written without the condition, the checker refuses the line: 'Ill-formed type: FullRange[\I\] The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Index.'
